title: Computational biological analysis reveals that HIF-1 and FoxO signaling pathways influence cognitive impairment in patients with depression.
authors: Zhuo, Chuanjun; Zhang, Ying; Zhang, Qiuyu; Yang, Lei; Chen, Ximing; Ma, Xiaoyan; Li, Ranli; Wang, Lina; Tian, Hongjun; Mao, Fuqiang
one_liner_zh: 该文用计算生物学方法分析抑郁认知障碍相关靶点网络与通路，并虚拟筛选药物与靶蛋白结合，但核心是蛋白-小分子对接而非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无TF-DNA结合建模或AI/物理模拟方法，仅边缘相关。
abstract: Cognitive impairment, a common symptom in patients with depression, significantly affects social functioning. Currently, no recognized treatment exists for depression-related cognitive dysfunction. The study aimed to use computational biology methods to investigate the potential molecular mechanisms underlying cognitive impairment in depression and identify potential antidepressants that may mitigate this impairment. Targets associated with depression and cognitive impairment were obtained from GeneCards and OMIM. Overlapping disease targets were integrated to generate a PPI network, and hub targets were identified using network topology metrics. KEGG pathway enrichment analyses were conducted using the DAVID database. Finally, core targets enriched in key signaling pathways were virtually screened for interactions with antidepressants. Of the 1621 overlapping targets identified, 46 key targets were selected based on topological parameters in Cytoscape software of a KEGG enrichment analysis. The analysis revealed that the HIF-1 and FoxO signaling pathways may contribute to depression-induced cognitive impairment via 13 target genes. Virtual screening of these 13 core targets against various antidepressants identified mosapramine as having strong binding affinity to the core targets, including AKT3, EGFR, IL6, INS, MAPK1, MAPK3, and PIK3R1, with docking scores of -7.6 to -12.9 kcal/mol. Based on our results, the HIF-1 and FoxO signaling pathways may influence cognitive impairment through multiple targets, and mosapramine may alleviate cognitive impairment in patients with depression via these targets and pathways. These findings provide a foundation for the modification and optimization of antidepressant drugs to improve the treatment of cognitive impairment in patients with depression.
abstract_zh: 认知障碍是抑郁症患者常见的症状，显著影响其社会功能。目前，针对抑郁症相关认知功能障碍尚无公认的治疗方法。本研究旨在利用计算生物学方法探讨抑郁症认知障碍的潜在分子机制，并识别可能缓解该障碍的潜在抗抑郁药物。从GeneCards和OMIM数据库中获取与抑郁症和认知障碍相关的靶点。整合重叠疾病靶点以生成PPI网络，并利用网络拓扑指标识别核心靶点。使用DAVID数据库进行KEGG通路富集分析。最后，对富集于关键信号通路中的核心靶点进行虚拟筛选，以评估其与抗抑郁药物的相互作用。在识别的1621个重叠靶点中，基于Cytoscape软件中的拓扑参数和KEGG富集分析，筛选出46个关键靶点。分析显示，HIF-1和FoxO信号通路可能通过13个靶基因参与抑郁症诱导的认知障碍。对这13个核心靶点与多种抗抑郁药物的虚拟筛选发现，莫沙帕明与核心靶点（包括AKT3、EGFR、IL6、INS、MAPK1、MAPK3和PIK3R1）具有强结合亲和力，对接分数为-7.6至-12.9 kcal/mol。基于我们的结果，HIF-1和FoxO信号通路可能通过多个靶点影响认知障碍，而莫沙帕明可能通过这些靶点和通路缓解抑郁症患者的认知障碍。这些发现为抗抑郁药物的修饰和优化提供了基础，以改善抑郁症患者认知障碍的治疗。
